resources.string: Usage and app health

Sends anonymous counts to Google Analytics for Firebase: which kinds of pages and features you use, whether connecting, sending, setup, agents, the background service and updates work, how fast the app starts and how smooth pages are, memory warnings, and ranges for your phone's memory, free storage, CPU and WebView version. Also sends timings to Firebase Performance Monitoring: how long app start, connecting, the first reply, setup steps and starting an agent take. Only fixed words, ranges and numbers, with a random install ID, your phone model and Android version. No code, conversations, files, addresses, keys or advertising ID.
Send crash data automatically
Ask me after a crash
Crash reports

Sends crash reports to Google Firebase Crashlytics: the kind of error and where in the app's code it happened, never its message, the last steps you took as short words, and why Android ended the app last time. No code, conversations, files, addresses, keys or advertising ID.
What we collect
Usage and Crash reports are off until you turn them on. See exactly what each one sends.
This version does not send usage and app health yet. Your answer is kept and used once it does.

When usage is on, usage reports go to Google and to our own Umami analytics server, hosted with Railway. Umami stores no IP address or identifier of the person, and its anonymous visitor hash changes every month and cannot be turned back into your address or your device. The app itself sends only fixed words, ranges and its version and build, never free text. Google adds, on its own, a random install ID, the phone model and the Android version; our Umami server gets none of those. Turning usage off deletes unsent reports.

Whether connecting to a server worked, the kind of failure and how long it took, and when you choose to connect a computer
Why a connection dropped and whether it came back
Whether sending a message worked or waited in the queue, how you made it (typed, spoken or attached), which agent, and how soon the first reply came

How each turn ended (done, finished with nothing to show, stopped, error, connection lost or no answer to an approval), how long until you saw a first reply and until the agent first showed any sign of work, how long it took, how many tools it used and whether it recovered from a dropped connection

What kind of request you were asked (run, edit, read, web or a question), your answer or that a saved choice answered it or the run was stopped, where you answered (conversation, home, a notification or a widget), and how long it waited. Never the command, file or question itself
A long wait’s stage, duration and cause: confirmed silent thinking, a running tool, a retry, a missed or broken connection, an unconfirmed quiet connection, or unknown

Which kinds of pages and features you use, the first reply after you agreed (and that you had seen one before agreeing, never anything about it), how long a visit lasts and how many messages you sent in it
How far you got in your first steps (opened the app, set up, connected, sent a message, got a first reply) and roughly how long after you agreed. Each step is counted once
Which kind of suggestion you tapped on a new conversation, and your one-word answer to what you want help with. Never a suggestion’s words or what it asks

How fast the app starts. Also the previous process exit (app_exit): its fixed reason (exit_reason) and, when Android knows it, whether the process was in the foreground (foreground, yes/no)

How smooth pages are (the share of late and slow frames, and frozen frames), the screen’s refresh rate, and in the conversation what was going on (a reply arriving, scrolling, a menu or sheet open, the keyboard up or nothing)
Memory warnings from Android

Ranges for your phone’s memory and free storage, its processor type and WebView version, whether notifications are allowed, and the kind and version of server you use. Our own Umami server gets only the app version and build number, app language with its region (such as ar-EG), Android main version and device class (phone or tablet). Google Analytics also receives, on its own, a random install ID, the phone model, the Android version and the screen size.
The kind of error and where in the app’s code it happened, never its message

When the app’s process ended unexpectedly last time, a report named process_exit with its fixed reason (exit_reason). A stop you asked for, which Android names user_requested, is never sent as a report: it is only counted with Usage and app health
Your last 30 steps, as short words such as chat.send

The app version, how it was installed, the kind of server, whether this phone’s server is running, how many connections are open, the server version, and the kind and code of a report. Google Crashlytics also adds, on its own, the phone model, the Android version, free memory and storage, whether the phone is rooted and a random install ID

What you write about the problem, the last time the app closed unexpectedly, the app and Android versions, a memory range and the kind of server, with keys, addresses and paths blanked. No log and no conversation. You see all of it and choose Send or Cancel.

Your prompts and replies, recorded voice audio (transcribed on the device by a speech model downloaded from huggingface.co so the audio never leaves the phone, or by Android's own on-device speech recognition on Android 12 and later, offline preferred, where Android's privacy terms for that service apply), file names or paths, web addresses, host names, IP addresses, error message text, keys or tokens, the advertising ID or the Android ID

Sends anonymous counts to Google Analytics for Firebase: which kinds of pages and features you use, whether connecting, sending, setup, agents, the background service and updates work, how fast the app starts and how smooth pages are, memory warnings, and ranges for your phone's memory, free storage, CPU and WebView version. Also sends timings to Firebase Performance Monitoring: how long app start, connecting, the first reply, setup steps and starting an agent take. Only fixed words, ranges and numbers, with a random install ID, your phone model and Android version. No code, conversations, files, addresses, keys or advertising ID. Usage reports also go to an analytics server we run ourselves: Umami, hosted with Railway. Umami stores no IP address and no identifier of the person. It uses the connection address once to work out a coarse location. It keeps an anonymous visitor hash that changes every month; the hash cannot be turned back into your address or your device. Umami gets the app version name and build number, the app language with its region (such as ar-EG), the Android main version number (for example 16) and whether the device is a phone or a tablet, and nothing else about the device: not the screen size, the model, the maker, the time zone or any device or installation ID.

If you agree, usage and app health reports go to Google Firebase and our own Umami server hosted with Railway. Crash reports go to Google Firebase. Umami stores no IP address or personal identifier. You can change each choice in Settings › Privacy and data.
